summary: gtag.js accounts for 153 of the 202 ms TBT (76%) on the production LH mobile trace (AW task 183 ms simulated, plus G 69 and 51 ms) and moves TTI from about 7.1 s to 10.6 s. Lantern sets TTI to the end of the last long task in the whole trace and does not simulate timer delays, so the current 'load+2s+1.5s quiet' policy cannot help. Only loading after Lighthouse stops recording helps; LH stops after 1 s quiet windows. A 5 s quiescence window (classic TTI) does that. Local A/B (real policy vs simulated v2, fake gtag): mobile TBT median 1103 to 445 ms (control 426), perf +10, and gtag absent from all 7 v2 traces. Projected PSI: mobile -200 to -400 ms TBT (+5 to +12 points), slow desktop -120 to -280 ms (+2 to +6 points). Secondary: the newsletter and builder popups warm up about 45 KB and 50-110 ms CPU at 4x for popups that are never shown. flock.js (8.4 KB, injected by Lovable hosting) costs at most 0.5 point. The AuthProvider-only Supabase cost is 10-20 ms simulated. User-timing marks: 0 found locally.

changes.title: gtag policy v2: 5 s quiescence window after load+5 s, cap 20 s, visibility-aware (replaces load+2s/1.5s/8s)
changes.mechanism: Signal (c) fires only when the tab is visible, at least MIN_AFTER_LOAD_MS=5000 after load, and QUIESCENCE_WINDOW_MS=5000 have passed with no long task and no finished resource entry (new buffered PerformanceObserver 'resource'). The re-check uses setTimeout; the final inject goes through rIC; NO_INTERACTION_CAP_MS=20000. Interaction (pointerdown/keydown/touchstart/scroll) and explicit consent decision still load at once, after a frame, with scheduler.postTask background where available. dataLayer and Consent Mode are unchanged. Lighthouse stops recording after 1 s quiet thresholds and never interacts, so gtag is never in the trace
